events.text: A visiting alchemist from a neighbouring isle remarks, over wine, how well the house has lasted. The remark is idle. But {ot4_holder}, keeper of {ot4_post}, looks at you and does not look away, and at the far table {npc} and {ot4_b} each find something urgent to pour. choices.text: Send them in together, and let them share the desk

choices.text: Stay in the Lotus Infirmary all day, out of reach

events.text: Two sets of banners hang from the Cloud Library on feast day, which is irregular, and neither is yours. {npc} had gold-and-white made for the occasion; {ot4_b} found jade-and-grey. The visiting disciples from the other isles took sides within the hour, and have now been seen trading spirit stones on the matter. You find yourself standing between them, in your own courtyard, as an unwelcome neutral.

choices.text: Take the gold-and-white down yourself, as an example

effects.log: It is meant as even-handed. It is taken as a hint that jade-and-grey has won, and the next day {npc} does not come to practice.

choices.text: Hang both banners from your own window

effects.log: It is an eccentric gesture, and it works for a month.

choices.text: Order the jade-and-grey banners burned

effects.log: They are burned in the court. {ot4_b} watches until the last thread, and does not speak to you again for a long time.

choices.text: Go on to the ceremony and ignore them both

effects.log: The ceremony proceeds. The banners hang. Everyone remembers you ignored them.

events.text: {ot4_holder}, keeper of {ot4_post}, asks for an audience, and in the audience says that the isle will not survive a divided house. He has watched it happen to another, he says, in the first century of his service. He wishes nothing for himself. He wishes only that you decide before the others decide for you. His hands, as he says it, are not entirely steady.

choices.text: Thank the keeper, and say you are close to choosing {npc}

effects.log: He bows, relieved and unconvinced. By nightfall the whole isle has the news.

choices.text: Thank the keeper, and say you are close to choosing {ot4_b}

effects.log: He bows, relieved and unconvinced. By nightfall the whole isle has the news.

choices.text: Thank the keeper, and bring both of them in to hear it

effects.log: The three of them hear him out. The two rivals nod in the same direction for the first time in years.

choices.text: Thank the keeper, and say a decision made in haste is a decision made twice

effects.log: He leaves with the look of a man who has been very patient, for a long while, in vain.

events.text: A forged letter appears on the desk of {ot4_holder}, in {npc}'s hand, offering a spirit-stone tithe from the Stone Vault to a rival isle in exchange for a quiet word. It is a clumsy forgery. It is also, plainly, the work of {ot4_b}'s circle, who do not think anyone will examine the seal. {npc} learns of it from a third party at breakfast and turns pale before the tea cools.

choices.text: Prove it false, in public, and back {npc}

choices.text: Let the rumour stand, and back {ot4_b}

effects.log: The rumour stands. {npc} is quietly sidelined. It is a hard thing to watch, and you watch it.

choices.text: Have {ot4_b} confess, and bear the consequence

effects.log: The confession is dragged out in an afternoon. {ot4_b} is humbled in front of the elders of the isle.

choices.text: Let both find out what the other is capable of

effects.log: They do. Neither is the same afterward.

events.text: A sword-disciple of {npc}'s party is found at the foot of the Gate of Mist at dawn, unharmed and very frightened, with a note sewn into a sleeve in {ot4_b}'s style. There was a plan, the note says, for the next feast day, and it was not a friendly one. The elders of the isle are in your hall by midmorning. No one will speak first. Everyone wants to be told what has happened.

choices.text: Name {npc} the heir, and place {npc} under your guard

effects.log: It is done in the full hall. {ot4_b} is not seen again until the evening, and is calm.

choices.text: Name {ot4_b} the heir, and answer the note publicly

effects.log: It is a hard thing to do, and it is done. {npc} leaves the hall without a word.

choices.text: Seal {ot4_b} in the Stone Vault until the feast is past

effects.log: The Vault is cool and dry. {ot4_b} is not harmed, and not forgiven.

events.text: The wine at the feast of the Lotus Infirmary is not what it should be. {ot4_holder} catches the taste first, and by luck, and the cup is knocked from {npc}'s hand before any harm is done. In the ensuing confusion, three attendants of {ot4_b} are found to have left by the east pier. The cup was meant for one of the two. No one is sure which, and each believes it was them.

choices.text: Stand beside {npc}, and name the culprits

effects.log: You stand, and you name them, and the hall holds its breath. {npc} does not weep, but nearly.

choices.text: Stand beside {ot4_b}, and say the cup was a plot of {npc}'s own

effects.log: It is a grim accusation. It is half believed, which is worse than fully.

choices.text: Say it was no one's doing, and eat from the same pot

effects.log: You eat. Nobody dies. It is the oddest scene of the century.

choices.text: Seal the east pier, and wait for the attendants

effects.log: The attendants are brought back in a week. They say nothing at all.

events.text: Late at night, someone cuts the rope bridge to the western terrace, with {npc} and a half-dozen of {him} on it. They are caught by two guards on the cloud-mooring, bruised and breathless. The rope was cut cleanly, with a tool from the Stone Vault. There is a small cry of rage from {ot4_b}'s quarter before the dawn, and a longer silence in the hall.

choices.text: Name {npc} now, so none can say it was for nothing

effects.log: The hall hears it. {ot4_b} bows, correct as a ruled line.

choices.text: Name {ot4_b}, so that the cutting was at least a lesson

effects.log: It is a cold choice, and the house feels how cold.

choices.text: Order {ot4_b}'s attendants to the lower isles

effects.log: They go. {ot4_b} takes the order like a slap, and says nothing.

choices.text: Repair the bridge yourself, and tell no one

effects.log: You repair it, rope by rope, in the dawn. It is a strangely calming labour.

events.text: The cloud-corridors of the isle ring with swords. Not a duel, but a brawl, a score of disciples from both parties meeting in the passage under the Cloud Library and finding no reason to stop. {ot4_holder} has barred the great doors from the inside. The elders of the isle stand at the end of the hall in white robes, unmoving, as if they were already portraits.

choices.text: Step between them, and name {npc}

effects.log: You step between. The swords stop in the air. Your voice rings in the corridor, and {ot4_b} is the first to lower a blade.

choices.text: Step between them, and name {ot4_b}

effects.log: You step between. The swords stop in the air. Your voice rings in the corridor, and {npc} is the first to lower a blade.

choices.text: Break the party of {ot4_b} with your own hand

effects.log: It takes four breaths. The corridor is silent. {ot4_b} is carried out and does not look back at you.

choices.text: Send the elders of the isle between them, in a line

effects.log: The elders walk into the swords like old, slow clouds. The swords stop. It is humbling for all.

events.text: A section of the isle's outer wall has been scorched black. It was done by sword-qi, from within, at night. Both parties were asleep, or claim to have been. The Lotus Infirmary has been used as a barracks for the wounded. {ot4_holder}, who keeps the Gate of Mist, has been told by both sides that the gate is theirs. It stands shut. Everything else is open.

choices.text: Name {ot4_b}, and have the gate opened in that name

effects.log: The gate opens. {npc}'s party watches in silence, and then in rage, and then in bewildered quiet.

choices.text: Strip {ot4_b} of any post, and set a guard

effects.log: It is done in an hour. The scorched wall is the last thing {ot4_b} looks at.

choices.text: Let the gate stay shut, and watch who moves

effects.log: The gate stays shut for nine days. Both parties starve a little, in pride.

events.text: The great hall of the isle has become two camps divided by a strip of polished floor that nobody will cross. Disciples eat apart, practise apart, bathe in different springs. The old cook has gone on strike, and will feed only the infirm. When you enter the hall both parties rise, in perfect unison, and then glare at each other for rising at the same time.

choices.text: Cross the strip, and stand with {npc}

effects.log: The whole hall hears the sound of your boots. It is a most informative sound.

choices.text: Cross the strip, and stand with {ot4_b}

effects.log: The whole hall hears the sound of your boots. It is a most informative sound.

choices.text: Stand on the strip itself, and eat there

effects.log: You eat your lunch standing on the line. It is an undignified meal. By evening the strip has a table across it.

choices.text: Let the old cook's strike run its course

effects.log: The strike lasts a week. It is the only thing the two camps ever agree on.

choices.text: Say that you wish it could have been otherwise

effects.log: {npc} nods. It is, by then, all there is to say. The mist rises.

choices.text: Say nothing, and walk with {him} to the end of the stair

effects.log: You walk. At the end, {npc} bows, and goes down alone. It is as it should be.

events.text: The house splits at dawn. {npc} stands on the western pier with a hundred disciples and three barges, and the banner of a new house, still creased from the chest. No violence. No curses. Only a very polite parting, in which both sides carefully avoid looking at each other. {He} bows, and boards, and the barges lift on a clean wind.

choices.text: Wave from the pier, and wish {him} well

effects.log: {npc} does not wave back. But the barge does not leave until you stop.

choices.text: Watch from the Cloud Library, unseen

effects.log: You watch until the barges are lost in cloud. You do not know what you feel, and you do not try to name it.

events.text: The Gate of Mist has two keys, and for the first time in the isle's long history they are not on the same ring. {npc} takes the one that opens outward. A hundred disciples follow {him} in silence down the White Stairs. The elders of the isle stand along the rail like rooks, and the old cook sets out two lanterns instead of one.

choices.text: Stand at the head of the stair, and bow

effects.log: They bow back, correctly, in two long lines. Nobody speaks. It is a farewell without a word.

choices.text: Close the Gate behind them, softly

effects.log: You close it. The sound is small, and long.

events.text: The quarrel over {ot4_seat} ends without you. One of the two is gone from it, by death, or by distance, or simply by giving up, and the other goes on alone. The elders of the isle say the matter has resolved itself. The Cloud Library has stopped keeping two piles of scrolls. It is a very quiet morning, and nothing in it is yours to decide.

choices.text: Hold a small service for the house

effects.log: You hold it, at the Lotus Infirmary, with a handful of old friends. It is warm and brief.

choices.text: Turn back to your own work

effects.log: You turn back to it. It is steady, and it waits, and you are glad of it.

events.text: No one tells you the quarrel is over. You learn of it from the tea: the old cook, serving the usual morning, brings one cup for each side and a third for the empty seat. It is a gentle, wordless report. The house goes on, as houses do, and you find you do not know whether to be relieved or ashamed.

choices.text: Drink the cup for the empty seat

effects.log: It is a bitter tea, and you drink it all. The cook nods.

choices.text: Ask the cook what she saw

effects.log: She tells you, plainly and briefly. It is more than anyone else had dared.

choices.text: Let the two of them part, and found their own places

effects.log: The two go. The compound is smaller by half in the morning, and quieter.

events.text: The two have been called to the stores. {ot4_holder} has laid out everything {ot4_seat} holds: the seal, the keys, the old charters, a purse of silver. Between the two heaps stands you. choices.text: Take the seal yourself, and let neither have it

effects.log: You take it. The two look at you as though you had died.

choices.text: Give each a portion, and let them part

events.text: {npc}, whom you passed over, comes to you at dusk in the Scripture Hall and bows lower than courtesy needs. There is no bitterness in it, and no forgiveness either. {He} says only that the place has chosen and {he} will serve it. Then {he} asks, in a very steady voice, for leave to take the long road to the coast for a few years.

choices.text: Grant it, and give {him} a letter of the house

effects.log: {npc} takes the letter. It is perhaps the first gift in a long time that has not felt like a verdict.

choices.text: Ask {him} to stay, and name {him} to a senior post

effects.log: The post is a good one. {npc} accepts it after a long pause, and holds it very well.

events.text: The passed-over one waits for you at the gate at the hour you walk there each evening. {npc} does not speak at first. The dust of the road moves between you. Then {he} says, quite simply, that {he} has made peace with it, and that the peace is not the same as being glad. You hold that sentence a long time.

choices.text: Say that you wish it could have been otherwise

effects.log: {npc} nods. It is, by then, all there is to say. The dust settles.

choices.text: Say nothing, and walk with {him} to the end of the lane

effects.log: You walk. At the end, {npc} bows, and goes down alone. It is as it should be.

events.text: The place splits at dawn. {npc} stands at the east gate with a hundred pupils and three carts, and the banner of a new school, still creased from the chest. No violence. No curses. Only a very polite parting, in which both sides carefully avoid looking at each other. {He} bows, and goes, and the carts roll off down the lane.

choices.text: Wave from the gate, and wish {him} well

effects.log: {npc} does not wave back. But the last cart does not turn the corner until you stop.

choices.text: Watch from the Scripture Hall, unseen

effects.log: You watch until the carts are lost in the dust. You do not know what you feel, and you do not try to name it.

events.text: The main gate has two keys, and for the first time in its long history they are not on the same ring. {npc} takes the one that opens outward. A hundred pupils follow {him} in silence down the lane. The elders stand along the wall like rooks, and the old cook sets out two lamps instead of one.

choices.text: Stand at the head of the lane, and bow

effects.log: They bow back, correctly, in two long lines. Nobody speaks. It is a farewell without a word.

choices.text: Close the gate behind them, softly

effects.log: You close it. The sound is small, and long.

events.text: The quarrel over {ot4_seat} ends without you. One of the two is gone from it, by death or distance or simple weariness, and the other goes on alone. The elders say the matter has resolved itself. The record-keeper has stopped making two piles. It is a very quiet morning, and nothing in it is yours to decide.

choices.text: Hold a small service for the place

effects.log: You hold it, in the Scripture Hall, with a handful of old friends. It is warm and brief.

choices.text: Turn back to your own work

effects.log: You turn back to it. It is steady, and it waits, and you are glad of it.

events.text: No one tells you the quarrel is over. You learn of it from the soup: the old cook, serving the usual supper, ladles a bowl for each side and a third for the empty place. It is a gentle, wordless report. The place goes on, as places do, and you find you do not know whether to be relieved or ashamed.

choices.text: Eat the bowl for the empty place

effects.log: It is a thin soup, and you finish it all. The cook nods.

choices.text: Ask the cook what she saw

effects.log: She tells you, plainly and briefly. It is more than anyone else had dared.

events.text: {npc} comes up the White Stairs unannounced, the way they used to come late to the morning lesson, and sits down across from you without asking. They have heard about the quarrel over {ot4_seat}; the whole of the Floating Isles has. "You said once you would send for me," they say. "So I am sparing you the letter. Tell me whose back to stand at."

choices.text: Send {npc} to stand with {ot4_a}

effects.log: {npc} goes to {ot4_a}'s side of the house the same evening, and the elders of the isle count the steps.

choices.text: Send {npc} to stand with {ot4_b}

effects.log: {npc} takes a room near {ot4_b}'s quarters. Two old desks and a long friendship have chosen a side.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to keep out of it, as a friend

effects.log: {npc} laughs, a little hurt, and stays for tea instead.

events.text: A letter comes on a paper crane from {npc}, who sat beside you for years at the side school and still writes in the same cramped hand. The crane says they have watched {ot4_a} and {ot4_b} from a neighbouring isle, and that a house divided is a house that needs one more honest person in its halls. They will come to whichever side you name.

choices.text: Write back: stand with {ot4_a}

effects.log: The next crane is {npc} in person. They walk straight to {ot4_a}, and the halls notice.

choices.text: Write back: stand with {ot4_b}

effects.log: {npc} arrives with one bag and goes to {ot4_b}. The other side watches them pass.

choices.text: Write back that this one is yours to carry alone

effects.log: The crane that comes back only says: then I will wait. {npc} does.

events.text: {npc}, who studied beside you at the side school before either of you was a god, comes to your temple with no offering and no herald. "The lesser gods of your temples are choosing between {ot4_a} and {ot4_b}," they say, "and so are their worshippers. Let me choose too. Tell me which one, and I will stand there where the prayers can see me."

choices.text: Send {npc} to stand with {ot4_a}

effects.log: {npc} kneels in {ot4_a}'s shrine at the evening prayers. The faithful talk of nothing else for a season.

choices.text: Send {npc} to stand with {ot4_b}

effects.log: {npc} lights a lamp at {ot4_b}'s altar, and leaves it burning.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to keep their light out of it

effects.log: {npc} nods, and lights a lamp for you instead, which is worse and kinder.

events.text: A prayer reaches you that is not a prayer: it is {npc}, an old classmate from the college, speaking the way you both spoke when the masters were not listening. They have heard {ot4_a} and {ot4_b} quarrel over {ot4_seat}. They offer what they have, which is their name and their patience. They will put both behind whichever of the two you choose.

choices.text: Answer: stand with {ot4_a}

effects.log: {npc} comes to {ot4_a}'s hall. The quarrel has one more voice in it, and it is a steady one.

choices.text: Answer: stand with {ot4_b}

effects.log: {npc} sits at {ot4_b}'s table from the next feast on. The other side sets one fewer cup.

choices.text: Answer that a friend is worth more outside it

effects.log: {npc} sends back a single word of agreement, and stays where they are.

events.text: {npc}, who shared your bench at the side school all those years, walks in through the gate of {ot4_seat} with mud on their boots. The elders are choosing between {ot4_a} and {ot4_b}, they say, and so is half the world you made. "You told me you would send for me. I came before the letter. Where do you want me?"

choices.text: Send {npc} to stand with {ot4_a}

effects.log: {npc} sits down beside {ot4_a} at supper, and the long table goes quiet for a moment.

choices.text: Send {npc} to stand with {ot4_b}

effects.log: {npc} goes to {ot4_b}'s rooms with their one bag. Everyone sees which way they walk.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to stay out of it

effects.log: {npc} shrugs, stays the night, and leaves you a good bottle on the way out.

events.text: A message comes by a carter's boy from {npc}, your old benchmate at the side school: they have heard of the quarrel over {ot4_seat} all the way out on the far roads. They are no one great, they write, but they are honest, and everybody there knows it. They will come and stand with whichever of the two you name.

choices.text: Send word: stand with {ot4_a}

effects.log: {npc} arrives within the month and goes to {ot4_a}. The elders count one more on that side.

choices.text: Send word: stand with {ot4_b}

effects.log: {npc} arrives and sits with {ot4_b}. People who trusted {npc} begin to trust {ot4_b} a little.

choices.text: Send word to keep out of it

effects.log: The carter's boy brings back a note: as you like, and I am here if you change your mind.
